subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: Should OpenClaw accept `@openclaw/mxc-sandbox` as a first-party installable Windows sandbox plugin with the current native dependency graph and upstream MXC argv-carried config transport?
rationale: The remaining blocker is not a narrow code repair: it is a security/product boundary choice about native binaries, install-script dependencies, preview MXC APIs, and what OpenClaw will support as an official sandbox backend.

options.title: Approve current boundary after secops review
options.body: Allow the exact current head after secops/admin approves the dependency graph and maintainers accept the preview SDK transport as an intentional prerelease boundary.

options.title: Pause for non-argv transport
options.body: Keep the PR open until MXC SDK or the plugin can pass sensitive config without placing the envelope in native executor argv.

options.title: Keep MXC outside first-party packaging
options.body: Close or redirect this to external plugin ownership if maintainers do not want to support the native dependency and sandbox boundary in OpenClaw releases.

recommendation.title: Approve current boundary after secops review
recommendation.body: Allow the exact current head after secops/admin approves the dependency graph and maintainers accept the preview SDK transport as an intentional prerelease boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR is assigned to him and the decision combines first-party product direction with a security-sensitive dependency acceptance.
